content: Write a marketing email re-engaging customers who haven't logged in for 90 days.

# Re-Engagement Email: 90-Day Inactive Customers

## Subject Line Options
1. It's been a while, [First Name] — here's what you've missed
2. Your [Product] account is still here (and it's gotten better)
3. We saved your spot
4. 3 things that changed since your last visit
5. Still interested? Just checking. 👀

**Preview text:** Your account, settings, and data are exactly where you left them.

---

## Main Email

**Subject:** It's been a while, [First Name] — here's what you've missed

Hi [First Name],

We noticed you haven't logged into [Product Name] in a few months. No hard feelings — life gets busy.

But a lot has changed since [Month of last login], and we think a few things might be worth a second look:

**[Feature/Update #1]** — [One-line benefit, e.g., "Reports that used to take 20 minutes now build themselves."]

**[Feature/Update #2]** — [One-line benefit]

**[Feature/Update #3]** — [One-line benefit]

Your account is exactly as you left it — [settings, saved data, integrations, team members] all intact. One click and you're back in.

[**Log back in →**]

If [Product Name] isn't the right fit anymore, we'd genuinely like to know why. Just hit reply — a real person reads every response, and it takes 30 seconds to tell us what went wrong.

Thanks for giving us a shot in the first place,

[Sender Name]
[Title], [Company]

*P.S. — [Optional incentive: "Come back this week and we'll extend your plan by 30 days, on us." or "Want a 15-minute walkthrough of what's new? Grab a time here."]*

---

## Shorter Alternative (Plain-Text Style)

**Subject:** Still interested?

Hi [First Name],

Quick one: you haven't logged into [Product Name] since [Month]. I'm trying to figure out if that's because:

1. You're busy and just haven't gotten back to it
2. Something wasn't working the way you expected
3. You've moved on to something else

If it's #1 — [your account's right here]. If it's #2 or #3, hit reply and tell me. I'd rather hear it than guess.

[Sender Name]
[Company]

---

## Notes for Deployment

- **Personalize the "what's new" section** by segment. A dormant power user needs different reasons to return than someone who never finished onboarding.
- **Lead with value, not guilt.** Avoid "We miss you!" framing — it centers your needs, not theirs.
- **Save the discount for email 2 or 3.** Leading with a coupon trains customers to churn for deals and devalues the product-led reason to return.
- **Suggested cadence:** Day 0 (this email) → Day 5 (social proof / customer story) → Day 12 (incentive + clear last-chance framing) → sunset from the active list.
- **Include a visible unsubscribe and a "pause emails" option.** Cleaning your list improves deliverability more than squeezing a few extra sends out of unengaged contacts.
- **A/B test the subject line first** — it drives the majority of open-rate variance in win-back campaigns.
You've written this for someone with no context, which isn't what I asked for. Rewrite it for a reader who already knows the background.

## Subject Line Options
1. Your [last project name] is still sitting there
2. [First Name] — [specific thing they built] is 80% done
3. Picking up where you left off
4. Your team's been using it without you
5. Quick question about [Account Name]

**Preview text:** Nothing's been deleted. Nothing's expired.

---

## Main Email

**Subject:** Your [last project name] is still sitting there

Hi [First Name],

[Dynamic: "Your [project/report/workflow name] hasn't been touched since [date]."]

Not chasing you about it — just flagging that it's still live, still connected to [integration they set up], and still doing [whatever it does] in the background. If that's intentional, ignore this.

If it's not, two things changed that affect your setup specifically:

**[Change #1 tied to their configuration]** — the workaround you were using for [thing] isn't necessary anymore.

**[Change #2 tied to their plan or usage tier]** — [specific implication for them].

[**Open [project name] →**]

And if you've moved to something else, tell me what and why. I'll stop emailing and you'll have done me a favor.

[Sender Name]
[Title]

---

## Shorter Alternative

**Subject:** Quick question about [Account Name]

[First Name] —

[Teammate name] logged in [X] times last month. You haven't since [date].

Is that a deliberate handoff, or did something break for you specifically?

[Sender Name]

---

## Third Option — Data-Led

**Subject:** [X] [items] processed while you were away

[First Name],

Since [last login date], [Account Name] has:

- [Metric 1 — e.g., processed 1,240 tickets]
- [Metric 2 — e.g., saved an estimated 31 hours]
- [Metric 3 — e.g., flagged 8 exceptions nobody reviewed]

That last one's the reason I'm writing. [Specific consequence of the unreviewed items.]

[**Review flagged items →**]

[Sender Name]

---

## Notes

- The behavioral merge fields (last project, teammate activity, unreviewed items) are what make these work. Without live data feeding them, fall back to the shorter version — a vague "we miss you" performs worse than a two-line note.
- The third option only sends to accounts with genuine accrued activity. Firing it at a dormant single-seat account with zero data reads as automated and undermines the other two.
- Third option assumes multi-seat or ongoing automation; skip it for solo, manual-use accounts.

---

*Assumed "knows the background" means the recipient — an existing user with account history — so I've cut the product framing and written these to reference their specific configuration and usage rather than re-explaining the tool. Say the word if you meant something else and I'll adjust.*
This runs much longer than it needed to and buries the point. Cut it to about half the length and lead with the main point.

**These only work if live merge fields feed them.** Without real behavioral data, use the short version — a generic "we miss you" underperforms a two-line note.
